_comment: Backup registry of browser-engine archive URLs, kept in this repo so upstream/CDN deletions never strand a version. One entry per engine -> chromium version -> platform. Empty url = not installable on this host (either never captured, or the capture is gone — see each entry's note). etag (when known) identifies the exact build behind a (possibly reused) CDN key.
_mirror: Engine archives are mirrored to https://github.com/pdtkts/tunsia-engine (public, one release per Chromium build). Upstream's CDN keeps only ONE archive per platform key and overwrites it in place on every bump, so any build not captured in this repo is unrecoverable — 148/149/152/156 are all gone this way. Widevine stays on the upstream CDN key because its etags are byte-stable across engine bumps.

shardx._source: Mirrored: https://github.com/pdtkts/tunsia-engine/releases/download/<tag>/<asset>. Upstream origin was the shared CDN key https://pub-e57a7c60f6934eb09a6600bf2fc59cdc.r2.dev/<key>, which holds only the CURRENT build behind each platform key.

148.0.7778.216._note: NOT INSTALLABLE — archive never captured. Upstream's key ShardX-Windows.zip was overwritten by 149 long before this registry started mirroring, so no copy of the 148 archive survives anywhere. The build still runs on machines that extracted it under the legacy flat layout; it cannot be downloaded. Get it from such a machine's runtime/ dir if you ever need it back.

windows-x64.note: etag recorded from a local manifest.json browser_etag (the 148 Windows build); no archive behind it any more

149.0.7827.103._note: NOT INSTALLABLE — archive never captured, and the upstream key now serves a later build. The urls below used to point at the live CDN key; that key's content advanced 149 -> 152 -> 156 -> 157, so they would have installed the WRONG engine under this version's name. Blanked deliberately: a wrong build under the right name is worse than no build. If you have 149 on disk from an earlier install (runtime/shardx/149.0.7827.103/), mirror it from there to restore installability.

156.0.8078.48._note: NOT INSTALLABLE — archive lost. Upstream shipped four builds of 156 (etags eb861fc080cb30f6e84bee3b449abee1-24, b3e367936b0725d0c16f53e1c31b2925-25, 894255f8e59920f3684f75ca8bb62968-25, 9418227a94434221a847160fb0938ca4-25), all behind the same ShardX-*.zip key, and none was mirrored before the key advanced to 157. Verified 2026-11-06: the key serves etag 12d7b8cdc67fdd42ebe803731334f295-26 (the 157 build) and ShardX-156.zip 404s. This is the case the mirror now exists to prevent.

gpm-chromium._source: GPM Login Global manages its own Chromium cores under %APPDATA%/GPMLoginGlobal/Browsers/ChromiumCore_v<N>/. No direct download URL — the GPM Login app installs/updates cores. Detection only (gpm_runtime::scan_cores). Record core versions here for reference; url stays empty.

windows-x64.note: installed via GPM Login app; not downloadable standalone

zeroclaw._source: GitHub releases https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/releases/download/<version>/<asset>. Pinned to the zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw release ONLY (single official repo — impersonation notice, evidence-packet §3). sha256 is MANDATORY for this engine (fail-closed, unlike shardx): a version entry with a blank sha256 is not installable. This is the SHA-256 of the EXTRACTED main binary (`zeroclaw` / `zeroclaw.exe`), NOT of the archive asset — the archiver computes it from the unpacked release contents, and the installer's hash gate (`sha_digest` over the staged binary) verifies against exactly that value. Record the release tag in note.
